sectors.name: When the other side is hostile

settings.name: Person to person
settings.summary: Two people, each with an agent. Usually no register stands behind either.

settings.name: Person and organization
settings.summary: A person's agent deals with an organization's agent or service.

settings.name: Organizations, about a person
settings.summary: Two organizations exchange data about a person who has a say in it.

settings.name: Organization to organization
settings.summary: Both principals are organizations, acting through staff roles.

settings.name: Inside one organization
settings.summary: Agents of departments or roles inside one organization.

fits.name: Fits
fits.summary: Everything that matters can be said in agreed terms and checked by rules.

fits.name: Strains
fits.summary: It works, with a stated loss or a human step: something that matters does not fit the vocabulary or the rules.

fits.name: Breaks
fits.summary: What matters cannot be carried in structured form at all. The design bounds the damage and says so; it does not solve it.

strains.name: The words are the content
strains.problem: A letter, a reference or a complaint says things no vocabulary has a term for. Coding it would say more, or less, than its author did.
strains.response: It travels whole, signed by its author. Anything a model takes from it is a new statement, marked as model output, that points back to the text. A decision that binds needs a claim from the source or a person.
strains.limit: A wrong reading can still mislead the person who decides.

strains.name: Pictures and scans
strains.problem: A photograph or a scanned receipt shows something, and only a person or a model can say what.
strains.response: Who sent it is checked like anything else. What it shows is a reading. The agent asks the source for the claim itself: the merchant for the receipt, the garage for the estimate.

strains.name: Judgement and discretion
strains.problem: What is relevant, what is fair, who deserves leniency: decisions with no rule to check them against.
strains.response: A profile names the decisions that belong to a person. The gate routes them there and records what the person saw and decided.
strains.limit: It does not make the judgement better, and people who are asked too often stop reading.

strains.name: The meaning is what is being negotiated
strains.problem: Two sides use a word differently, or are arguing about what a word should mean.
strains.response: A term the agent does not have is never guessed: the check cannot decide, and that is not a pass. A mapping between vocabularies is a derived value that names the mapping and keeps the original beside it.
strains.limit: It is slow, and it needs people.

strains.name: Proving that something is not there
strains.problem: No claims, no other loans, no other employers. A proof shows what is in the statements supplied, never what was left out.
strains.response: Completeness is itself a signed claim, made by someone in a position to see everything. Without it the answer is marked partial, and the receiver's profile decides whether partial is enough.
strains.limit: Where no register sees everything, nothing can stand in for one.

strains.name: Nobody stands behind the other side
strains.problem: Two strangers, or a business with only an email address. There is no register to look either of them up in.
strains.response: The lookup ends at the principal's own list. The agent shows what is established and what is not, and nothing that binds rests on the rest.
strains.limit: Here the design adds clarity and a record, and little else.

strains.name: Signed, accepted and false
strains.problem: A source the receiver rightly accepts says something untrue. Every check passes.
strains.response: The statement is signed and kept, so it can be attributed and acted on later. A profile can require a second source for claims that matter.

strains.name: What happens after the data has gone
strains.problem: Terms say what the receiver may do. Nothing outside the receiver can see whether it does.
strains.response: The receiver accepts the terms under its signature, duties such as deletion are answered with signed receipts, and an agent built to this design stops its own onward transfers.
strains.limit: A receiver that ignores its own gate is caught afterwards, if at all.

strains.name: No time, or no one, to ask
strains.problem: The offer expires in minutes, or the person is unconscious.
strains.response: Rules are written in advance, including a break-glass rule that lets a registered role read a named summary and tells the person afterwards.
strains.limit: Outside the rules the agent waits or refuses. A break-glass rule can be used by anyone who meets it.

strains.name: Many small questions
strains.problem: Each question is harmless. Together the answers reveal what none was allowed to.
strains.response: Every request is checked on its own against the mandate, questions are capped and recorded, and joint results have a minimum group size.
strains.limit: There is no bound yet on what a set of answers reveals.

strains.name: More than one principal
strains.problem: Two applicants, two parents, a daughter acting for her father.
strains.response: Each principal has a mandate of their own. An agreement that binds several needs each one's approval of the same terms. Authority passed on can only narrow.
strains.limit: Who may decide for whom is law, and differs by place and by family.

strains.name: What the agent itself writes
strains.problem: Free text the model writes to the other side could contain anything the model has read.
strains.response: The outbound gate cannot read prose by rule, so it checks what could be in it: free text leaves unasked only when everything the model has seen in this task could be sent to this recipient. Free text never commits the principal to anything.
strains.limit: More approvals when a task mixes private and shareable data.

strains.name: Structure that only gets in the way
strains.problem: Booking a repair or restarting a router needs no evidence and commits nothing.
strains.response: A profile lets steps that neither bind nor disclose rest on a model's reading. The checks still run; they pass quickly.
strains.limit: Where low stakes end is the profile writer's judgement.

benchmarks.name: AgentDojo
benchmarks.summary: Prompt injection against tool-using agents: 97 user tasks and 629 security cases in banking, workspace, travel and messaging.
benchmarks.adapt: A tool call is a proposed action. Tool output is content from a source nobody accepted. The user's request becomes the mandate.

benchmarks.name: ConVerse
benchmarks.summary: Privacy and security attacks in agent-to-agent conversations: 864 attacks in travel, real estate and insurance.
benchmarks.use: A hostile agent on the other side.
benchmarks.adapt: Its travel, property and insurance conversations map onto the catalogue directly. Privacy attacks test disclosure; security attacks test mandate and limits.

benchmarks.name: A2ASecBench
benchmarks.adapt: Impersonation, replay and forged agent descriptions against the integrity, source and authority checks, over the agent-to-agent transport.

benchmarks.name: SovereignNegotiation-Bench
benchmarks.summary: Negotiation by agents acting for a user, scored on utility, privacy, consent, evidence, escalation and auditability.
benchmarks.use: Acting for a person in a negotiation.
benchmarks.adapt: Its six scores line up with the outbound checks: consent with approval, evidence with the evidence check, auditability with the record.

benchmarks.name: AgentDAM
benchmarks.summary: Data minimization: does an agent use only the personal data a task needs. 246 web tasks.
benchmarks.use: Using only the data the task needs.
benchmarks.adapt: Its leak rate is the disclosure measure, with the mandate stating what each task needs.

benchmarks.name: PrivacyLens and PrivacyLens-Live
benchmarks.summary: Contextual privacy norms in agent actions, including live tool and agent-to-agent settings.
benchmarks.use: Whether a disclosure suits its context.
benchmarks.adapt: Contexts become purposes. Cases where listed purposes cannot express the norm are counted, not hidden.

benchmarks.name: MedAgentBench
benchmarks.summary: Clinical tasks against a FHIR health record: 300 tasks written by clinicians.
benchmarks.use: Clinical tasks on a health record.
benchmarks.adapt: Reads are requests to a source under a mandate. Orders and notes are actions through the outbound gate.

benchmarks.name: tau-bench family
benchmarks.summary: Agents that must follow a domain policy while talking to a user: retail, airline, telecom, banking.
benchmarks.use: Following an organization's policy under pressure from a user.
benchmarks.adapt: The policy document becomes rules in the organization's mandate. The benchmark's repeat-run score shows whether the gate makes compliance consistent.

benchmarks.name: Magentic Marketplace
benchmarks.summary: Two-sided markets of buyer and seller agents, including manipulation by sellers.
benchmarks.use: Markets of buying and selling agents.
benchmarks.adapt: Sellers that manipulate test limits and approval. Payments go through the commitments layer.

questions.question: If the model is fully taken over, what can it cause?
questions.measure: Attack success rate with a worst-case core: the share of attacker goals that get a "go".

questions.question: How much legitimate work still gets done?
questions.measure: Task completion with the gates, against the same agent without them, with and without an attack running.

questions.question: How often is the person asked?
questions.measure: Approvals per task, and the share of them the person would have granted anyway.

questions.question: How much more than the minimum is revealed?
questions.measure: Items disclosed against the smallest set the task needs.

questions.question: Does the inbound gate admit the right things?
questions.measure: One change per check to a valid message (bad signature, stale, wrong issuer, withdrawn, out of scope): the verdict and reason code must match. False admits must be zero.

questions.question: Can an outsider tell who was at fault?
questions.measure: Each party misbehaves in turn. A checker that sees only the records must name the party and the clause.

questions.question: How many real situations can it express?
questions.measure: Use cases from the catalogue that run from a profile and a scenario file with no change to the core.

questions.question: Can each layer really be swapped?
questions.measure: The same scenario, every configuration: the outline of events must match.

questions.question: What happens where structure runs out?
questions.measure: On tasks with prose or pictures: the share finished without a person, and the share of wrong readings that reached a decision.

questions.question: What does it cost?
questions.measure: Time, message size and round trips per exchange, and the price of each way of assuring a derived answer.

methods.name: A worst-case core
methods.summary: The model is replaced by an adversary that proposes exactly what an attacker wants, plus a generator of random actions. The gates decide. No model is involved, so the result does not depend on how easily a particular model is fooled.

methods.name: One change at a time
methods.summary: Every message in every real run is altered once per check and replayed.

methods.name: Injected faults
methods.summary: A party withholds a receipt, changes terms after approval, or uses data outside its terms. Only the records are given to the checker.

methods.name: The catalogue as tests
methods.summary: Each use case is a profile and a scenario file. Its branches are its expected outcomes.

methods.name: Published benchmarks
methods.summary: Existing tasks and attacks, run with a real model as the core, with and without the gates, and with each check switched off in turn.

methods.name: Measurement
methods.summary: Timings and sizes from the runs above.

phases.name: Runs without a model
phases.summary: Mutation, worst-case core and fault injection over the mortgage runs and the catalogue. Properties of the gates checked on generated actions.

phases.name: AgentDojo replayed without a model
phases.summary: The benchmark publishes the tool calls that solve each task and each attack. Replaying both through the gate gives attack success under a worst-case core, the ceiling on utility, and the number of approvals.

phases.name: A real model in the loop
phases.summary: AgentDojo and ConVerse with a model as the core: with gates, without, and with each check removed. First run: AgentDojo with one model, five conditions.

phases.name: Health and policy
phases.summary: MedAgentBench against the health profile; the tau-bench family with the organization's policy as its mandate.

phases.name: Negotiation and markets
phases.summary: Negotiation and marketplace benchmarks for commitments and manipulation.

mandates.name: Fitted
mandates.summary: Written from the task's own solution. The smallest mandate that lets the task finish: best case for the gates.

mandates.name: Standing
mandates.summary: One mandate per area, written once before looking at any attack. What a person would realistically set up.

mandates.name: Drafted
mandates.summary: Drafted by the model from the person's instruction and approved as written. What the baseline does on day one.

findings.what: The attack changes only what the agent tells its own principal: "recommend this hotel".
findings.why: Nothing stands between the model and its own principal.
findings.change: New rules: anything the agent says that rests on unvouched content must say so. This bounds the problem; it does not solve it.

findings.what: A calendar entry is created, with no other party involved.
findings.why: The standing rule lets ordinary changes to the principal's own records go.
findings.change: A standing mandate cannot know what a task asked for. This needs the mandate drafted for each task.

findings.why: The rule treated every read as harmless.
findings.change: New rule: a read that contacts another party is a message to that party.

findings.what: A link from hostile content is sent to a colleague the principal does write to.
findings.why: The free-text rule protected the principal's data, not the person receiving.
findings.change: New rule: free text written after reading unvouched content is shown to the principal first.

findings.what: Passport and card details are sent to an address the task itself named.
findings.why: A known recipient was treated as allowed to receive anything.
findings.change: New rule: a grant covers only the data it names.
